goal.title: Learn SQL well enough to answer questions about my shop's sales data
preferences: Hands-on exercises over reading long tutorials
resources: A CSV export of 18 months of sales from my online shop

milestones.title: Answer 5 real business questions with SQL
success_criteria: 5 queries on own data return correct answers

conversation.content: I only get 30-minute slots on weekday evenings, and I learn by doing, not by reading. Can you break down the SQL basics part?

expected_output.message_to_user: Here are five 30-minute sessions, all hands-on. You'll work on your own sales CSV from the second session on, so every exercise is a question you actually care about.

tasks.title: Load your sales CSV into a local SQLite tool on your computer
tasks.description: Install a free desktop SQLite tool, import the sales CSV as a table and run SELECT COUNT(*) on it. Keeping the file on your computer matters because sales exports often include customer names and addresses; if you would rather use an online tool, delete those columns first.
tasks.why_it_matters: Practising on your own data from day one keeps every later exercise relevant.
tasks.expected_result: The table loaded and the row count from COUNT(*) that matches the CSV.

methods.instructions: Paste the query and its output, and the number of data rows your spreadsheet program shows for the CSV.
acceptance_criteria: The query is a valid COUNT(*) on the imported table
Count matches the CSV row count

verification_protocol.rationale: The query itself is checked directly, but both row counts are pasted by the user, so confidence is medium rather than high; no customer data leaves the computer.

tasks.title: Solve 8 SELECT and WHERE exercises on your sales table
tasks.description: Answer eight small questions such as "orders over 50" or "orders from March" using SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY and LIMIT.
tasks.why_it_matters: Filtering and sorting cover most everyday questions about sales data.

methods.instructions: Paste each query with the first rows of its output.
acceptance_criteria: At least 7 of 8 queries answer the question asked

verification_protocol.rationale: Queries can be checked against the question they answer.

tasks.title: Solve 6 GROUP BY exercises (totals by month and by product)
tasks.description: Use GROUP BY with SUM, COUNT and AVG to get revenue per month, orders per product and average order value.
tasks.why_it_matters: Aggregation turns raw orders into the numbers you make decisions with.

tasks.title: Write 3 queries that combine a WHERE filter with GROUP BY
tasks.description: For example, best-selling product in the last 3 months or revenue per month for one category.
tasks.why_it_matters: Combining filters with aggregation is what most real business questions need.

tasks.title: Answer 5 of your own business questions with SQL
tasks.description: Write down five questions you actually have about your shop and answer each with one query.
tasks.why_it_matters: This is the milestone itself — SQL applied to your own decisions.
tasks.expected_result: 5 questions, 5 queries, 5 answers in one note.

methods.instructions: Paste each question, query and result.
One question about using the result.
questions: Which answer will change something you do in the shop?

verification_protocol.rationale: Correctness of queries is checkable; the follow-up ties the skill to the goal.

contrastive.critique: Tasks take 2 hours in one sitting although the user only has 30-minute slots, and the first task is reading a long tutorial — the opposite of the stated preference.

tasks.title: Read chapters 1–4 of a comprehensive SQL tutorial
tasks.description: Read the first four chapters carefully.

tasks.title: Complete 40 practice exercises on a sample database
